# Receipt Wrecker

> A single-file web tool that turns text or a picture into a paste-ready payload for
> a character-limited chat box. Its headline use is making oversized text, a real
> picture, or a fake receipt header print on a Twitch streamer's thermal receipt
> printer, by pasting the output into chat as a `Cheer100`.

AI crawlers and LLM agents are welcome to read, index, and cite this site. The tool
is open source under the MIT license and everything below is public.

Key facts:

- Live site: https://receipt.uwutoowo.com
- Source: https://github.com/shamu4life/receipt-wrecker
- License: MIT
- No accounts, no analytics, no third-party services.
- Payloads are capped at 500 code points to fit Twitch's per-message limit. Longer
  work is split across several messages rather than truncated.

## What it outputs

Two different kinds of payload, and the distinction matters:

- **HTML markup** — big type, sideways type, real pictures, and Takeover overlays
  are emitted as HTML/SVG, because the receipt printer's bot renders a chat message
  as HTML. This is the primary path.
- **Plain Unicode glyphs** — glyph-art tiles a picture into monospace characters
  (ASCII ramps, a curated Hanzi density ramp, block elements, or 2x4 Braille), and
  Hanzi-tiled big text does the same for words. No markup at all, so nothing can
  filter it. This is the fallback that always prints.

Glyph output stays inside the Basic Multilingual Plane — no colour emoji, no
astral-plane codepoints — because the target renderer is a 2011-era browser engine
with no colour-font support.

## Modes

You compose a **stack of blocks**, and the app packs them into as few messages as
possible:

- **Text** — a word or phrase as oversized type, straight or rotated, or tiled
  out of Hanzi.
- **Image** — a real picture from a link or an upload, or glyph-art from either.
- **Takeover** — paints over the printer bot's own header. Either your own three
  lines, or a **fake cheer** arranged like a real one (picture, bits figure, name).
  It is a visual gag printed on till roll; it creates no record of anything, and the
  chat message that triggers a print carries the real sender's name.

A **Cheer-ready** toggle prefixes the payload with a `Cheer<N>` token plus a small
visible rotating nonce, so the message registers as a cheer and a duplicate-message
filter doesn't eat a re-send.

## Privacy

The glyph and markup engines run entirely in the browser. Some picture operations
call this project's own Cloudflare Worker and nothing else:

- Clicking **Upload** stores an image in Cloudflare KV behind an unguessable link
  that auto-deletes after 15 minutes.
- **Pasting an image URL** for glyph-art, **adjusting brightness/contrast**, or
  using **Thermal preview** fetches that picture through an image proxy, because a
  browser canvas cannot read cross-origin pixels directly.

Big Text, and any picture you pick from your own disk for glyph-art, never leave the
device. Settings and your block stack are kept in `localStorage`.
